```{r setup, results='hide', output=FALSE}
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tmap)
```


"Lines" is the theme for day 2 of the #30DayMapChallenge. I figured I should do a follow up to [yesterday's post about public bookcases](https://haraldkliems.netlify.app/posts/2026-11-01-30daymapchallenge-day-1-points/). After making my post I went out for a walk to collect photos of a few more bookcases. I half-jokingly told my SO that maybe I should use a [traveling salesman algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travelling_salesman_problem) to optimize my Sunday walk. Well, I didn't do it before my walk, but why don't I do for today's challenge?

I'm using the [GraphHopper Route Optimization API](https://docs.graphhopper.com/openapi/route-optimization). They have a free tier available but you do need an API key.

# Construct the query

I'll use an updated dataset of the bookcases, taking into account the bookcases for which I added photos yesterday and a few new ones I found. To speed things up I filter for nodes without photos right in the Overpass query:

```
  [out:json][timeout:60];
  {{geocodeArea:Madison, Wisconsin}}->.a;
  node["amenity"="public_bookcase"][!panoramax](area.a);
  out center;
```

This results in 228 bookcases without photo. 

```{r}
bookcases <- st_read("data/overpass_export.geojson")
```

There doesn't seem to be an up-to-date package for interacting with the Graphhopper route optimization API endpoint from R and so I need to use `httr2`. The API needs json with the locations as its input. I'm going to do this quick and dirty, and just copy and paste together some stuff. Here's the code to create the list of destinations (called "services" in the API) from the Overpass output:


```{r json-helper, eval=FALSE}
location_json <- bookcases |> 
  # head(3) |> 
  mutate(id = str_remove(id, "node/")) |> 
  rowwise() |> 
  mutate(address = tibble(
    location_id = "test",
    lon = st_coordinates(geometry)[1],
    lat = st_coordinates(geometry)[2]
  )) |> 
  select(id, name, address) |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  jsonify::to_json() |> 
  clipr::write_clip()
```

Then there's a bunch of json to specify the type of vehicle, start location, etc. I save all this and the locations in [json file](data/bookcase.json). 

Now we feed the file to the API and save the response:

```{r api-query}

base_url <- "https://graphhopper.com/api/1/vrp"
key <- Sys.getenv("GRAPHHOPPER_API")

req <- request(base_url) |> 
  req_url_query(
    key = key) |> 
  req_body_file("data/bookcase.json", type = "application/json") |> 
    req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE)   # let us inspect 400s ourselves

resp <- req |> req_perform()
```

Next I parse the response into two `sf` objects: One multi-linestring of all segments between the bookcases, as the crow flies. And one dataframe with the ordered stops themselves. I'm really not good at parsing and converting deeply nested `json` and used an LLM to help with this part of the code. 

```{r parse-response}
solution <- resp_body_json(resp)

# multilinestring
route <- solution$solution$routes[[1]]

coords <- map(route$activities, \(a) c(a$address$lon, a$address$lat)) |>
  do.call(rbind, args = _)

segments <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(coords) - 1), \(i) coords[i:(i + 1), ])

route_sf <- st_sf(
  vehicle_id = route$vehicle_id,
  distance_m = route$distance,
  geometry   = st_sfc(st_multilinestring(segments), crs = 4326)
)

# stop locations
stops <- as_tibble(coords) |> 
  rowid_to_column(var = "stop") |> 
  rename(lat = V1, 
         lon = V2) |> 
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lat", "lon")) 
```


Now we can make a map! First a static map with just the lines:

```{r map-static, layout="l-body-outset"}

tmap_mode("plot")
tm_basemap(server = "Stadia.StamenTonerLite", api = Sys.getenv("STADIA_API_KEY")) +
  tm_shape(route_sf) +
  tm_lines(col = "orange", lwd = 2) +
  tm_title("Shortest bike route to all Madison public book cases that don't have a photo")
```


And now an interactive one that includes the stops and the number for the order they're in:

```{r map-interactive, layout="l-body-outset"}
tmap_mode("view")
tm_shape(route_sf) +
  tm_lines(col = "orange", lwd = 2) +
  tm_shape(stops) +
  tm_dots(fill = "darkblue", size = .4) +
  tm_text(text = "stop", col = "darkblue", xmod = .08) +
  tm_title("Shortest bike route to all Madison public book cases that don't have a photo")
```

The full route would be `r route$distance/1000` km (`r route$distance/1000*0.6213712` mi) long (the actual bike route, not the as-the-crow flies route shown on the map).
